conflicts: Weight, dimensions, warranty, needle system and presser foot lift did not appear in any accessible snippet. All left null; the janome.com product page could not be fetched.
Walking foot: the SMP accessory list does not include a walking or AcuFeed foot; an owner review confirms buying a $59 walking foot separately. Some retail bundles add one.
Price: not visible in accessible snippets. SMP shows only add-on packages ($99 sewing, $149 quilting). Left null.

ownerThemes.theme: A quilter's long-form owner review calls it fast and smooth with a wide throat that changes how quilts handle, but says the experience was poor until she bought the walking foot that is not in the box.
Review roundups flag that the default stitch length is long for piecing and that seam ends unravel unless shortened, and that the lack of a free arm limits cuffs and sleeves.
A PatternReview thread weighing the Skyline S5 against the MC6650 frames the choice as free arm and convenience features versus the 6650's longer flatbed and higher speed.

crossShop.why: The straight-stitch alternative with more speed and a 9 in arm for quilters who do not need utility stitches.
Janome buyers deciding whether a simple mechanical covers their heavy fabric work at a fraction of the price.
Lower-cost Juki straight-stitch head for the same quilting jobs.

editorial.verdict: A 10 in computerized flatbed with 170 stitches and a thread cutter for quilters who want one machine that pieces, quilts and still sews garments.
editorial.whoFor: Quilters and home sewists who want a long arm space and automated features without giving up zigzag, buttonholes and alphabets.
editorial.skipIf: You need a free arm for cuffs and sleeves, or you sew heavy canvas and leather often enough that a mechanical or industrial is the better tool.
editorial.keySpec: 1,000 spm · 170 stitches · 10 in arm · auto thread cutter
strengths: Dealers list a 10 in all-metal flatbed and 1,000 spm.
Automatic thread cutter and one-push needle plate change with two plates in the box.
Nine one-step buttonhole styles and two alphabets cover garment work a straight-stitch machine cannot.
weaknesses: No walking foot in the standard accessory list; owners buy one.
Weight, warranty and dimensions were not published in accessible sources.

checks.title: Walking or AcuFeed foot
checks.body: Confirm whether the bundle includes a walking foot. The standard SMP list does not, and one owner rated the machine poorly until she added one.

checks.title: Free arm need
checks.body: This is a flatbed. If you hem jeans and sleeves weekly, a free arm machine as a second unit may be needed.

checks.title: Package pricing
checks.body: SMP sells a $99 sewing package and a $149 quilting package on top of the machine. Check what is already in the box before adding either.

realCost: Extra bobbins and cone nets for large spools
